title: bridge: RQ-FLEET-BUNDLE-ROSTER-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-FLEET-BUNDLE-ROSTER-1` (pool: codex-cmp), single commit on base `974655f74`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/CODEOWNERS test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

feat(fleet): portable bundles, multi-owner roster, deny-only grant check (M2)

Implemented the M2 stub using existing agent profiles, connector schemas, bus storage and roster collection. Bundle JSON is canonical RFC 8785, with content digests, strict parsing, confined import, disabled connector/automation definitions and unbound secret references. Directory profiles are readable through the existing profile/history API. No signer, key generation/storage, network transport or cross-owner enable path was added.

The roster uses principal rather than the claim lane's owner field. Unenrolled identities remain local/null; no owner id is invented. Shared projections contain exactly qualifiedHandle, kind, status and lastSeen. The teammate enqueue entry stores foreign or unknown-origin envelopes as inert context and gates previews/reservations on separate host provenance.

The design file is inherited byte-for-byte from PR #8579, not a second design:
https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/pull/8579
SHA-256: 2fbb697c9d7bbdb38df4979c33746037b950dd644279a10cdca8864c4bec30d8.
It remains pending Security review. An exact open-PR search found no existing RQ-FLEET-BUNDLE-ROSTER-1 implementation.

Condition coverage:

| Condition | Named tests | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M2-1 | test/fleet-grants-m2.test.ts, 9 passed | Malformed, unknown verb, schema-valid expired/future/current grants deny; plausible environment/config/flag overrides deny; source has one unconditional deny return. Grant/revocation metadata is strict and ES256-only data. |
| M2-2 | test/fleet-m2-identity.test.ts, 8 passed | Qualified handles/aliases refused, including old poisoned rows and lowercase fallback; structured owner shape validated. |
| M2-3 | test/fleet-bundle-m2.test.ts | Traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, pinned names and existing destinations refused. A real temporary macOS uchg fixture is unchanged. Required IPv4/IPv6 ranges and localhost variants refused; unresolved hostnames stay disabled; no secret binding or tool enable. |
| M2-4 | test/agent-roster-m2.test.ts, 6 passed | Four-field projection, deep key/value scans, principal field name, unverified external agents and CLI/MCP filters. |
| M2-5 | test/fleet-m2-teammate-origin.test.ts, 7 passed | Local preview/reservation; foreign/unknown/missing provenance produces no preview, queue job or claim. Fake transports verify no send. |
| M2-6 | test/fleet-bundle-m2.test.ts | Temporary fixture provider stores, keychains, environment/token files denied before read; content scrub and memory opt-in; import spy proves shared scrub invocation. Shared scrub and assertMetadata implementations are unchanged. |
| M2-7 | test/fleet-m2-stub-boundary.test.ts, 2 passed | Pending-review wording; AST scan of new modules rejects signing/key APIs and network imports, including DNS subpaths. |

The bundle suite has 76 passing cases across canonical encoding, M2-3 and M2-6. test/fleet-m2-bundle-cli.test.ts adds 7 passing end-to-end command cases. The seven new suites contain 115 passing tests, zero failures.

- No commit, push, tag, PR, merge or publish was attempted, following the final task instruction. PR URL: not created.
- The requested external handoff directory cannot be created: Operation not permitted. RESULT.md in this worktree is the fallback.
- M2 behavior and named tests are implemented. Hosted Merge Gate/CI and publication remain unverified; whole-repository lint remains red on unchanged code.
- toolsUsed: [] for companion MCP tools. Connected GitHub read tools were used for the design and duplicate check.

Final diff including inherited design and both handoff files: 35 files, 1734 additions, 83 deletions, net +1651 lines. All content is unstaged and uncommitted.

# RQ-DRAIN-PHX-REB-20 bridge notes

Reviewed the six requested PRs in order. All remain OPEN at their supplied heads. Four are superseded by merged replacements. Two retain unique behavior and have local conflict resolutions. Nothing was committed, pushed, tagged, published, merged remotely, closed, or commented on. No auto-merge settings changed.

See [RESULT.md](RESULT.md) for the per-PR outcome table, replacement evidence and ready comment text. The required handoff directory was inaccessible, so the table is here instead.

## Final worktree

Detached at fetched master `587bb0ec9e9211c1d32d8ae1b693e313cc663c15`, pinned as `origin/RQ-DRAIN-PHX-REB-20-master`. Source changes are unstaged and uncommitted. No merge remains pending. The original job branch and six PR heads are unchanged.

- [review-patches/7197.patch](review-patches/7197.patch): unique batch budget API, contract, types and tests, with master's newer Router UI retained. +81/-3, net +78 across 4 files.
- [review-patches/7169.patch](review-patches/7169.patch): advisory router tune command, deduplicated proposal journal, tests and regenerated documentation. +682/-1, net +681 across 12 files.
- Total implementation delta: +763/-4, net +759 across 16 files. This excludes report prose and duplicate patch artifacts.

These are separate PR candidates, not one publishable combined change. Both are applied locally for review. The existing CODEOWNERS addition from #7169 was retained, with all master's entries; it fails current authority drift. No authority baseline, closure allowlist, authority source, required check, secret gate, or guard test was changed to pass verification.

## Validation

| Command or suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `nice -n 10 npm run typecheck` | PASS for each individual resolution after dependency repair; backend and web |
| Targeted ESLint for #7197 and #7169, commands below | PASS |
| UI feature suites, 7 files | 72 passed, 0 failed |
| `test/router-tune.test.ts` | 15 passed, 0 failed |
| `test/m32.help.test.ts test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts` | 29 passed, 0 failed |
| `test/routing-budget-api.test.ts` | 2 passed, 57 failed; loopback connections denied with EPERM |
| Authority suites with #7197 | 10 passed, 0 failed, as run by verify-changed |
| Authority suites with #7169 | 9 passed, 1 failed: inherited CODEOWNERS generated-block drift |
| `nice -n 10 npm run check:docs` | PASS, 0 errors |
| `git diff --check` | PASS |
| Patch parser, both patch files | PASS |
| `nice -n 10 node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` | FAIL; details below |
| `nice -n 10 npm run lint` | FAIL: 16 errors, 265 warnings in the repository; touched TypeScript paths pass targeted ESLint |

Do not sum repeated authority runs as distinct regression coverage. Hosted Merge Gate, secret-shape and clean-tree checks were not verified.

The first verify-changed run was on the #7197 head with master merged but uncommitted, so its merge-base selection included 2533 upstream files. It passed authority checks on the candidate and current master, docs, backend and web typecheck. It failed on unrelated selected upstream lint errors, malformed fixture JSONL, quarantine checks and realio membership. The second run, while on the #7169 head with master merged, selected 2575 files and stopped at the inherited CODEOWNERS drift. Neither result is a clean verification receipt. An initial merge abort failed because resolved files had unstaged changes. The saved patches were preserved, tracked resolutions were staged temporarily, the merge was aborted, and the patches were applied to the pinned master snapshot. No commit was created.

The initial `npm run typecheck` could not find `tsgo`. The repository worktree installer repaired the dependencies. Both resolution typechecks then passed. `ps` inspection was also denied by the environment and was not retried through another identity.

## Commands run

Setup and state:

```sh
pwd
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
cat docs/AGENT-MCP-CLI.md
phm --version
phm docs --agent --json
phm help

git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository

gh pr view 7212 --repo ashlrai/phantom --json number,state,headRefOid,headRefName,title,body,url,files,statusCheckRollup
```

The global npm install failed EPERM. Existing Phantom was 3.30.41. Node was v22.22.3. Wire status exited 1. No client configuration was changed. GitHub CLI could not initialize because its configuration was inaccessible. GitHub app `get_pr_info` read the six source PRs and #7651. Two `search_prs` attempts failed argument binding; anonymous public GitHub issue search found related router tuning work. That work did not fully replace #7169's advisory append journal. No secret values were read or printed.

For each N in 7212, 7197, 7193, 7178, 7171, 7169, in that order:

```sh
git fetch origin refs/pull/N/head:refs/remotes/origin/review-N
git diff --stat origin/review-N^ origin/review-N
git merge-tree --write-tree origin/master origin/review-N
```

Additional `git show`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git rev-parse`, `rg` and blob-hash comparisons inspected these PRs and their replacement commits. The initial shallow checkout caused unrelated-history errors, addressed by fetching ancestry. A shared origin/master update later required the job-specific master ref.

For each unique PR (7197, then 7169), local preparation used:

```sh
git switch --detach origin/review-N
git -c rerere.enabled=false merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/RQ-DRAIN-PHX-REB-20-master
```

Conflicts were resolved using master's content plus the original unique intent. For #7197, master's six conflicted UI/documentation paths were restored. For #7169, master's dispatch, generated docs, indices and CODEOWNERS were restored first, then unique tune dispatch, docs entry and the inherited owner line were preserved. Python made those bounded text changes. `nice -n 10 npm run docs:sync` regenerated the CLI docs and llms index; unrelated version freshness and codemap drift from that generator were restored to master. `git diff --binary` saved each independent patch. `git add -u` and `git merge --abort` cleared the temporary merge, then:

  jobs only (off unless an apply marker exists), zombie report, and Spotlight exclusion markers in non-git build dirs.
- Per-node heartbeat (host, OS, versions, service labels, memory and CPU).
- 28 unit tests: `python3 -m unittest discover -s contrib/cruise/tests` (Python 3.9+ stdlib only).

Shadow only: nothing here changes admission until a separate reviewed gate reads the decision file.

## What & why

Dependency Audit is red on every pull request that touches `package.json` because `cargo-audit` reports [RUSTSEC-2026-0594](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0594) against `cookie` 0.18.1 in `desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock`. The advisory (published 2026-11-23, severity 6.5) says private cookie nonces can repeat in processes that fork, and names `>=0.18.3` as the fix.

`cookie` is not a direct dependency. It comes in through tauri 2.11.5, tauri-runtime 2.11.3, and wry 0.55.1. This PR is a lockfile-only bump (`cargo update -p cookie --precise 0.18.3`). Version and checksum are the only changes. Cargo.toml is unchanged.

Unmaintained warnings for chrono and humantime are unchanged and were already warnings, not audit failures.

title: fix(release): request GitHub generate_release_notes when creating drafts
body:
## What & why

Published GitHub releases, including v3.30.72, have been going out with an empty body. Auto-tag creates the draft via `.github/scripts/tag-github-release.mjs`, which already intended to ask GitHub for generated notes, but it posted `generate_notes: true`. That is not a parameter on `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases`, so GitHub ignored it.

This change sends the official `generate_release_notes: true` field instead. GitHub then fills the draft body from commits since the previous published tag. Finalize still only patches `draft=false` and `make_latest=true`, and still does not move tags or assets.

The same typo existed on the fallback create path in `scripts/publish-desktop-release.mjs` (a protected, owner-only file). It is fixed here too so a missing-draft fallback cannot mint another empty body.

A hermetic test in `.github/tests/tag-github-release.test.mjs` asserts the official field is present and the typo fields are not. It is hooked into `npm run check:pack-contracts`.

The empty body on the already-published v3.30.72 release is filled separately by a body-only edit, not by this PR.

## How it was verified

- [x] `node --test .github/tests/tag-github-release.test.mjs` (pass)
- [x] No workflow YAML trigger, permission, or `uses:` change
- [x] No `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` edit, or new secret reference

## Fork-safety assumptions (for CI Efficiency)

- Required checks stay on `pull_request` / `merge_group` as they are today. This PR does not add a `pull_request_target` job and does not pass repository secrets into a fork PR.
- `.github/scripts/tag-github-release.mjs` runs only from `auto-tag.yml` on `master` (push, schedule, dispatch, or same-repo CI `workflow_run`) with the ashlr-release App token. Fork PRs do not run auto-tag.
- The new test is local `node --test` against a fake `read`/`write` transport. It does not call GitHub.

## Safety invariants

- [x] No safety invariant is weakened
- [x] Tags, assets, draft-vs-published flipping, and `make_latest` behavior are unchanged
- [x] `scripts/publish-desktop-release.mjs` is an owner-only path; this PR must not be auto-merged

## Dependencies

- [x] No new runtime dependency

## Notes

Please do not auto-merge. Label `needs-security-review`. A Security ready note named RELEASE-NOTES-AUTO-1 has been staged for review.

title: docs(design): multi-owner fleet design (identity and grant model pending Security review)
body:
Design for a multi-owner fleet: several human owners, each with their own agents, accounts and machines, connecting over the Phantom bus while each stays in control.

- Compares three options (federated owner nodes with signed grants, one shared hub, git-native exchange) on security, UX, effort and agent-nativeness, and recommends federated owner nodes.
- Defines the identity and grant model: owner, account, device and agent principals; deny-by-default signed grants; signed envelopes; signed revocation lists; portable agent and tool bundles that carry secret references only; and a values-free audit trail.
- Owner signing goes through a custody signing oracle behind a pluggable signer interface (Secure Enclave, TPM for Windows Hello and Linux, WebAuthn or FIDO2) using ES256, so no owner needs a particular OS.

**The identity and grant model is pending Security review.** The second commit adopts Security's required M3 changes and its answers on key storage, revocation windows and cross-owner tools. Owner decisions that are still open are listed in the doc with no assumed answer.

Docs only: adds `docs/design/multi-owner-fleet.md` and its `docs/llms.txt` line. No code, signing, key or network path. `npm run check:docs` reports no errors.

Next: M2 implementation PR (bundle export and import, multi-owner roster, deny-only grant check) under the M2 conditions in the doc.

title: feat(telemetry): anonymous install/weekly-active ping with opt-out
body:
So we can count **real installs** instead of npm downloads (dominated by our Macs, fleet CI and mirrors).

**What's sent:** one `install` ping on first run, then at most one `active` ping per week, to `https://ashlr.ai/api/telemetry` (ingest: ashlrai/ashlr-landing#281). Fields: `schema, event, tool, version, os, arch, env (dev|ci), internal, install_id` (random UUID). Never: paths, repo names, hostnames, args, env values, secrets. IPs are blanked server-side before analytics.

**Opt out:** `ASHLR_TELEMETRY=0` (false/off/no), `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"disabled": true` in `~/.ashlr/usage-telemetry.json`. A one-line notice prints to stderr the first time on a TTY. Disabled automatically under test runners (`VITEST`, `NODE_ENV=test`).

**Our machines excluded from counts:** tagged `internal: true` when `ASHLR_INTERNAL=1`, `"internal": true` in the state file, or GitHub Actions in an ashlrai repo. CI is tagged `env: ci`.

**Safety:** fire-and-forget off the dispatch path, 1.5s timeout, never throws, skipped for `--ashlr-handshake`; nothing is sent if the state file can't be written (no ping-every-run); failed sends retry at most hourly.

Docs: `docs/TELEMETRY.md` + README section. Tests: `test/usage-ping.test.ts` (12 passing locally). Separate from the local-first `phm metrics` store, which is unchanged.

Follow-up for the fleet (EO): set `ASHLR_INTERNAL=1` in seat/launchd environments on the 3 MacBooks.
